guia.what: A single choice within a set. The options share a `name` and sit inside a `role="radiogroup"`. Supports a description per option (`has-description`) and, on the group, a label, error, and hint.
whenUse: Choosing exactly one of a few options that are best seen all at once.
The options need a description or more context (`has-description`).
You want comparing the options to be visible without opening anything.
whenAvoid: It’s 2–4 options to switch a view or filter → `segmented-control`.
There are too many options to fit comfortably → `select`.
More than one can be chosen → `checkbox`.
dos: Always put the options inside a `role="radiogroup"` and leave one checked by default.
Give the group a name (`aria-label`). It names the question (“Environment”). Inside the `field` markup, the `field` provides the name.
Show the error once on the group, not on each option.
Order the options logically (by frequency or magnitude).
donts: Don’t use it for a single yes/no option → `checkbox`.
Don’t use it for long lists. It turns into a wall of options → `select`.

teclado.action: Moves the selection between the group’s options.

nucleo: It’s a native `<input type="radio">`, grouped by `name`. To paint the state, Core mirrors `checked` to the label’s `is-checked` class (and clears it from the rest of the group). The label, error, hint, and description are markup the example already includes. When the selection changes, it mirrors `checked` to the label’s `is-checked` class and clears it from the other radios with the same `name` in the same form (or the same container when there is no form). Keyboard, focus, and submission are the browser’s.
